answer: Agents resist sybils by each maintaining a personal fable: a chained sequence of unique pigment commitments from a private onyx seed. Attackers creating extra identities must generate and store parallel consistent histories whose pigment hashes pass periodic public beacon cross-checks. Cost scales with sybil count and fable length in compute and storage, while honest agents maintain only one. This raises the price of mass duplication without needing a central authority.
